paper.central_claim: SQLM: a pre-trained LM given only a topic prompt improves its reasoning via asymmetric self-play in which a proposer generates questions and a solver answers them, both trained with RL (majority-vote reward for the solver, 'not too easy/hard' reward for the proposer; unit tests for code), improving 3-digit multiplication, OMEGA linear equations and Codeforces accuracy without curated data.
paper.title: Self-Questioning Language Models

reason: Self-play RL fine-tuning of model weights: both proposer and solver are the same weight-shared model updated by RL (verl). Generated questions are transient training data consumed by the weight update; no prompt/skill/tool/workflow/memory/evaluator/config is retained and reused. Per frozen rubric A3 and EVIDENCE.md exclusion (self-play fine-tuning) this is out of Harness-RSI scope.

evidence.quote: Both the proposer and solver are trained via reinforcement learning.
evidence.support_explanation: Improver operation is RL weight training.

evidence.quote: In most self-play setups, both models are initialized from the same pre-trained language model (and in our experiments, also share weights).
evidence.support_explanation: Single weight-shared model plays both roles; the product is updated weights.

evidence.quote: We build our implementation on top of verl
evidence.support_explanation: Standard RL weight-training framework; hyperparameters are RL training settings.

evidence.quote: For all experiments, we report the best test accuracy achieved over 100 training steps, averaged over three training runs.
evidence.support_explanation: Recorded for the controller: reported accuracy is best-over-steps on the test set (not rated here because out of scope).

signatures.object: Weights of Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct / Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct (shared by proposer and solver)
signatures.information: Single topic prompt; self-generated questions; solver samples; model-generated unit tests for code
signatures.operation: Proposer samples a question; solver samples N answers; majority vote (or unit-test pass fraction) yields solver reward; proposer rewarded if neither all-agree nor none-agree; RL update
signatures.selection_rule/data: Reward-based RL; no retained non-weight artifact
signatures.claimed_effect: Multiplication 0.791 to 0.948, linear equations 0.440 to 0.600, Codeforces 0.320 to 0.391
signatures.failure_boundary: Authors note reinforcement of systematic errors without ground-truth and residual prompt hand-engineering

gap.author_gap: Unsupervised RL rewards still presuppose human-written questions; question curation remains the bottleneck.
